resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: South Orange Fire Prevention Bureau (Fire Official), within the Building and Code Enforcement Department
resale_co.lead_time: Expedited fees apply when the request comes 10 business days or less before closing; apply at least 11 business days ahead to avoid them.
requirements: Inspection by the Fire Official or inspector for compliance with N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 (smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms); smoke detector inspection is part of the CCO

Owner certifies all structures have valid zoning and building permits, registrations and certificates; the CCO verifies there are no open permits or violations unless a separate written agreement is attached
The CCO does not confirm zoning compliance; that needs a zoning verification letter, zoning permit or Certificate of Legal Nonconformity
No rubbish, debris or bulk garbage left on the property before the new occupancy
Application asks for buyer details, proposed closing date, realtor, room counts, accessory structures, house number visibility and any secondary power source (solar, generator, battery storage)
Secondary power source warning label within 18 inches of the main electric panel and meter, not handwritten
Monitored or low-voltage alarm systems need a current full NFPA 72 report from an alarm contractor or certified electrician
Someone must be at the property to give the inspector access (missed appointment fee otherwise)

fees.label: CCO, single family or condo/townhouse (online application)
Expedited fee, request 5 to 10 business days before closing (added to inspection fee)
Expedited fee, request 4 or fewer business days before closing (added to inspection fee)
fees.quote: 4 or Less Business Days - $100 Additional Fee

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online with the Village's Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application (GovPilot), linked from the Fire Prevention Bureau page and the Permit & License Application Forms page, and pay online. The owner, realtor or other contact can apply. Expedited fees count business days between receiving the request and the closing date, not counting the day the application is submitted. Fees are not refunded if the submission is incorrect. Office: 76 South Orange Avenue, Suite 302, (973) 378-7715.
resale_co.contact_title: Fire Official (also listed as Building Official)

evidence.quote: The issuance of CCO certificates for the change of ownership for both commercial and residential properties
The division is also responsible for inspections relating to issuing certificates of continued occupancy (for home sales) or habitability (for rentals).

A Certificate of Continued Occupancy shall be issued by the inspecting Official attesting that the residence, dwelling unit, room, suite or area meets or exceeds the requirements of N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19.
I understand that receiving this CCO certificate verifies that there are no open permits or violations, unless a separate written agreement is attached.
Expedited Fees - Based on the number of business days between receiving the request and closing date(not counting date application is submitted).

resale_co.notes: Fees come from Ordinance #2026-10 (adopted April 13, 2026), which restates Village Code 157-4 and 143-10, and match the online CCO application. The ordinance PDF is a scan with a text layer, so spacing in the quotes follows pdftotext output and minor OCR errors exist elsewhere in it. The Building Department page lists Anthony Grenci as Building Official (agrenci@southorange.org, ext. 7700) and the Fire Prevention Bureau page lists him as Fire Official (ext. 7703, firebureau@southorange.org). The ordinance also lists a separate 'Smoke Detector Compliance Certificate Fee' of $50.00 (see fire certificate). A Certificate of Habitability ($125.00 per unit online, $175.00 in the ordinance) is for rentals only and needs annual rental registration. Fee quotes from the ordinance are table rows from the pdftotext -layout output with spacing collapsed.

requirements: Smoke alarms UL 217 listed, no more than 10 years old; standalone battery alarms must be 10-year sealed
Smoke alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area; hardwired, interconnected and in-bedroom alarms depending on the year the house was built
Hardwired alarms stay hardwired; basement alarm within 10 feet of the base of the stairs
Carbon monoxide alarm on each level, and on sleeping levels within 10 feet of bedroom doors; UL 2034; battery, plug-in or hardwired
Secondary power source label within 18 inches of the main electric panel and meter
Monitored or low-voltage fire alarm systems need a current full NFPA 72 report

fire_cert.notes: In South Orange the smoke/CO alarm check for a sale is done inside the CCO inspection by the Fire Prevention Bureau, so most sellers pay the CCO fee. The ordinance also lists a separate $50.00 Smoke Detector Compliance Certificate Fee (157-12F); it is unclear when that applies instead of, or on top of, the CCO. The April 2025 residential requirements do not list a fire extinguisher, though the online CCO form has a 'Smoke Detector/Extinguisher Guidelines' tab whose text did not load.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations
other_items.detail: The CCO verifies there are no open permits or violations; the owner certifies all structures have valid zoning and building permits.

other_items.label: Zoning verification (optional)
other_items.detail: The CCO does not confirm zoning compliance. Zoning compliance can only be confirmed with a zoning verification letter or zoning permit from the Zoning Officer, or a Certificate of Legal Nonconformity from the Zoning Board.
